extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal education funds (elementary/secondary schools, postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and institutional administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and evaluative criteria for designing and operating Title IX grievance procedures, including rules on conflicts of interest/bias, investigation and decisionmaking processes, appeals, timelines, training, and use/disclosure of a single-investigator model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conflict of interest or bias for decisionmakers (§106.45(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(2) prohibits any person from serving as a Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker if they have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all decisionmakers including those who decide appeals of dismissals; if an investigator/decisionmaker develops a conflict or bias during the process, the recipient must designate someone else. The Department declined to identify roles that presumptively constitute a conflict; determination is fact-specific and left to recipients. Recipients must ensure Title IX personnel can serve without conflict or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment of complainants and respondents (§106.45(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must treat complainants and respondents equitably in the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle underlies choices about procedures, allocation of models (e.g., single-investigator vs. hearing), and must guide any determination about when different procedures apply to different complaint types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of not responsible until determination (§106.45(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must include a presumption that the respondent is not responsible for the alleged sex discrimination until a determination is made at the conclusion of the recipient's grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption is an explicit safeguard against prejudgment and supports impartiality in investigations and decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy protections for parties and witnesses (§106.45(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must take reasonable steps to protect the privacy of the parties and witnesses during the grievance procedures (subject to certain exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privacy protections should be balanced against investigatory needs; the regulation recognizes exceptions but requires reasonable safeguards to protect sensitive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of all relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence (§106.45(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations require an objective evaluation of all relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence and provide that credibility determinations will not be based on a person's status as a complainant, respondent, or witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes both inculpatory and exculpatory evidence; decisionmakers must evaluate evidence for persuasiveness under the applicable standard of proof and must not find discrimination unless persuaded by the evidence. Relevant and impermissible evidence are assessed consistent with §106.2 and §106.45(b)(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative evidence review process (§106.45(f)(3) and §106.45(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must review all evidence gathered through the investigation, determine what evidence is relevant and what is impermissible regardless of relevance, and the decisionmaker must evaluate relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence for its persuasiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The investigator identifies relevance and impermissibility; the decisionmaker assesses persuasiveness. If not persuaded under the applicable standard of proof, the decisionmaker must not determine that sex discrimination occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on investigator neutrality and impartiality (§106.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to train investigators on how to serve impartially, including by avoiding prejudgment of the facts at issue, conflicts of interest, and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is an express safeguard the Department relies on to mitigate bias risks. Training requirements also extend to designees and others carrying out Title IX duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights and appeal decisionmaker neutrality (§106.45(i) and §106.46(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer parties an appeal that, at minimum, is the same as it offers in other comparable proceedings; postsecondary institutions must offer appeals based on factors that would change material aspects of the matter, including procedural irregularity or decisionmaker conflict/bias that would change the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisionmakers for appeals must not have taken part in the investigation or dismissal. The Department declined to require live hearings during appeals but does not preclude them. Dismissal decisions and decisions to investigate are appealable if bias or conflict is alleged and would change the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and reasonable timeframes for resolution (§106.45(b)(4), §106.45(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must establish prompt and reasonable timeframes for their grievance procedures and have a broader duty to address complaints of sex discrimination in a 'prompt' manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations include protections against delay (e.g., §106.45(b)(4) and §106.46(e)(5)); permitting flexibility in procedural models is intended to avoid unnecessary burden while still ensuring prompt resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissive use of single-investigator model (§106.45(b)(2) discussion and §106.45(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations permit, but do not require, recipients to use a single-investigator model (investigator and decisionmaker may be the same person), and allow recipients to use single investigators, groups of investigators, or internal or external investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting the model is intended to provide flexibility to accommodate institutional size, resources, and structure. Use of the model is subject to all anti-bias/conflict and procedural safeguards; recipients retain discretion whether to adopt or limit the model. The Department declined suggestions to make its use consent-based or limited to resource-constrained recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and consistency requirements when using different models (§106.45(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient chooses to use different grievance procedure models (e.g., single-investigator for some complaints and live hearing for others), §106.45(b)(8) requires the grievance procedures to articulate consistent principles for how the recipient will determine which procedures apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must notify their educational community in advance when they will utilize a single-investigator model and ensure that determinations about which procedures apply treat complainants and respondents equitably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation required for informal resolution facilitator (§106.44(k)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.44(k)(4), the person who facilitates informal resolution cannot be the same person as the investigator or decisionmaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This separation protects against improper access, consideration, disclosure, or other use of information obtained solely through informal resolution, and preserves candid participation in informal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation to trained designees (§106.8(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may delegate duties under the final regulations to designees, including designees who are not employees of the recipient, provided implementation satisfies all regulatory requirements, including training designees consistent with §106.8(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using external or non-employee designees (e.g., outside investigators or adjudicators) is a permissible way to address conflicts of interest or resource constraints, but designees must be trained and procedures must meet regulatory standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural safeguards to test credibility and permit party response
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide a process that enables the decisionmaker to question parties and witnesses to adequately assess credibility when relevant, and parties must be allowed to view and respond to investigative reports and relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices suggested by commenters include asking parties to review interview summaries, ensuring all parties can view and respond to all information, and capturing responses in the investigation report. The regulations prohibit basing credibility on status and require objective evaluation of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to replace investigator/decisionmaker if bias or conflict arises during proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If an investigator develops a conflict of interest or bias during an investigation, the recipient must designate someone else to serve as the investigator and/or decisionmaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an operational safeguard to ensure ongoing impartiality: the recipient cannot allow a conflicted individual to complete decisionmaking and must have mechanisms to reassign roles when conflicts emerge.
